newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch govt to decide on Schiphol future in late 97.
newsitem.headline: Dutch govt to decide on Schiphol future in late 97.

text.p: The Dutch government's decision on the privatisation of Amsterdam Schiphol airport will not take place until late this year, at the earliest, said a Dutch Ministry of Transport spokesman.

Any decision on Schiphol will take place after a more general discussion on the future of aviation in the Netherlands, he said, and this discussion will not take place until the second half of the year.
Amsterdam Schiphol is owned by the Dutch government, which has a 76 percent share, Amsterdam City Council (22 percent) and Rotterdam City Council (two percent).
The general discussion is expected to focus on the prospect of constructing a second international airport in the Netherlands.
Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said last week that the government was positive about the privatisation of Schiphol.
Sources in the Netherlands felt that the decision on Schiphol was not likely until after the Dutch election, due next year.
